pr.title: Mark `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` mir-opt as unsound
pr.author: jieyouxu

analysis.originalLogic: GVN attempted the `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` rewrite for every aggregate rvalue whose type was a `Def`: in `gvn.rs`, `if let AggregateTy::Def(_, _) = ty && let Some(value) = self.simplify_aggregate_to_copy(rvalue, location, &fields, variant_index)`. This replaced constructing an aggregate from its fields with a copy of an already-available aggregate value. In the historical MIR, `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9)` was replaced by `_0 = copy (*_2)`, and `_0 = copy (*_1)` cases were similarly produced for nested clones.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The unsound rewrite introduced new dereferences of an existing place without checking for aliasing. It emitted `_0 = copy (*_2)` (a later re-read of the aggregate through `_2`) instead of rebuilding the aggregate from the already-read field `_6` as `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9)`. In the minimised case, `_2` is a reference obtained through `get(&v)` and aliases the `&mut Option<i32>` `_1`. After the original code writes `(*_1) = None`, the newly introduced `copy (*_2)` observes the overwritten `None`, so the function returns `None` rather than the captured `Some(col)`. The test document says the implementation "introduce[d] new dereferences without checking for aliasing".
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions that construct a `Def` aggregate (e.g. an enum variant such as `Option::Some`/`Option::None`, or a struct) from copied fields, where an equivalent aggregate value remains reachable through a reference/place that can alias memory mutated between the field reads and the aggregate construction/use. Typical Rust surface: a function taking `&mut T`, reading fields through a shared reborrow, then writing through the original mutable reference before returning the constructed aggregate. The behavioral difference appears at non-zero optimization (`-C opt-level=1`) but not at `-C opt-level=0`.
analysis.summary: Historical PR disables GVN's `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` mir-opt (added in #128299) by gating it behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`, because the rewrite can replace aggregate construction with `copy (*_place)` and thereby introduce aliasing-unsafe new dereferences. The regression is demonstrated with a `run-pass` UI test at opt-level 0 and 1, plus a GVN MIR-diff test showing the bad `_0 = copy (*_2)` rewrite.
analysis.trigger: With `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` enabled, GVN turns `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9)` into `_0 = copy (*_2)` even though `_2` aliases a mutable place (`_1`) that is overwritten with `(*_1) = None` before `_0` is used. The new re-dereference then reads the post-write value.
preconditions: GVN is running and `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` is enabled (at the time the default; now requires `-Zunsound-mir-opts`)
An equivalent aggregate value is reachable via a place/reference that may alias memory mutated between field reads and aggregate use
The aggregate's fields were copied out before the aliasing write takes place
Behavioral miscompile is exposed at a non-zero optimization level
pitfalls: Copying an existing aggregate value is not equivalent to constructing the aggregate when the source place can be mutated through an alias before use
Any rewrite that introduces new dereferences must prove they cannot observe intervening writes (aliasing check), otherwise the copy reads a different value
GVN can fold a field copy plus aggregate construction into a copy of the whole place; do not treat that as semantically preserving the captured field value
The bad rewrite changes `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9)` to `_0 = copy (*_2)` after `(*_1) = const Option::<i32>::None`; the overwrite and the aliasing reference are both needed
The PR only marks the pass unsound and does not revert the implementation, so the old transformation can still appear in MIR dumps when `-Zunsound-mir-opts` is supplied
Existing tests added by the original PR must be gated with `-Zunsound-mir-opts` rather than deleting them; non-pure-addition test edits were reverted
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `run-pass` UI regression test with two revisions, `-C opt-level=1` (release) and `-C opt-level=0` (debug), running the MCVE and asserting `min.unwrap()` does not panic; the minimized program uses `pop_min(vec![Some(1)])`. Also add a focused MIR test with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `-Zunsound-mir-opts`, emitting the before/after GVN diff and checking that the bad output contains `_0 = copy (*_2)` where the aggregate construction should retain `Option::<i32>::Some`. Compare actual value assignments in the decoded revisions rather than retaining names or comments.
evidence: The mir-opt can be re-enabled once this case is fixed.
This MCVE is included as a `run-pass` ui regression test in the first commit.
The mir-opt implementation is just marked as unsound but **not** reverted to make reland reviews easier.
Tests added by the original PR received `-Z unsound-mir-opts` compile-flags.
